title: A Letters for the Orchard
premise: Ansel Brightwater, a ghostwriter who vanished from his old life twelve years ago after a betrayal he never explained, is hired to write the memoirs of celebrated orchard-owner and rival author Wren Calloway—unaware she once loved him, or that the 'best mistake of their twenties' was each other. Stranded together by a snowstorm at her orchard estate, they are forced to confront the letter Ansel never sent, the identity Wren built to survive his disappearance, and the truth that her memoir deadline will expose them both. As Wren's found family of orchard workers closes ranks around her, Ansel must choose between loyalty to his employer's secrets and the truth that could win her back. In the end, Ansel publishes the memoir under both their names, forgives himself in the letter he finally delivers, and stays—not invisible, but rooted.
about_author: K. M. Ishikawa is a former orchard hand turned novelist who writes love stories about people who rebuild themselves in quiet places. They live between two coasts and one very opinionated dog.

chapters.title: The Ghost in the Margins
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. A ghostwriter who has spent twelve years being no one accepts a lucrative memoir commission from Wren Calloway, the rival whose name he can't stop typing into search bars at 3 a.m. When he sees her photograph on the contract, his safe small-step life cracks. Emotional beat: dread disguised as ambition—the past has found a forwarding address.

chapters.title: Snowfall at Hollow Orchard
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren arrives early to her family orchard to finish the book everyone expects of her, dreading the ghostwriter she's been assigned. The storm hits before she learns his name; a stranger knocks, snow-blind and familiar. She recognizes him before he speaks. Emotional beat: shock curdling into fury—twelve years of questions standing on her porch with luggage.

chapters.title: Twelve Winters
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Trapped by the storm, they circle each other through forced civility: shared meals, sharpened silences, the orchard workers watching like a jury. Flashbacks reveal the mistake of their twenties—a night, a promise, a departure without goodbye. Emotional beat: grief wearing politeness; every kindness costs them something.

chapters.title: What the Trees Remember
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Repairing storm-damaged apple trees together, Wren demands the truth and Ansel offers half of it: why he left, not what he was running from. His secret—that he ghosted the very book that made Wren famous, under another man's name—stays buried. Emotional beat: guilt sharpening; proximity makes lying harder than distance ever was.

chapters.title: The Found Family Table
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The orchard crew—her late mother's chosen family—tests Ansel with chores and stories, slowly adopting him despite Wren's objections. Wren realizes she's jealous not of their warmth toward him but of how easily he belongs somewhere. Emotional beat: longing reframed; home was never a place, it was always people.

chapters.title: Draft One, Confession Zero
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Interview sessions for the memoir become interrogations of the heart. Wren dictates memories that include him, watching him flinch as he transcribes his own erasure. He nearly confesses the ghostwriting; instead he writes it into a private letter he doesn't send. Emotional beat: the mirror moment—he sees the coward he became and hates the reflection.

chapters.title: Rival Lines
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren discovers an old acknowledgment page proving Ansel wrote her debut novel—and that her publisher knew, meaning her whole identity as an author was curated by others. She confronts him mid-blizzard; he admits everything except the reason he left her. Emotional beat: betrayal compounding betrayal; the person in the mirror is suddenly unrecognizable to them both.

chapters.title: The Letter Never Sent
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Rock bottom: Wren threatens to fire him and rewrite the memoir alone. Ansel finds his unsent letter from twelve years ago in his coat and finally reads it aloud—the truth about the threat that made him vanish to protect her career. Emotional beat: catharsis through confession; forgiveness of self begins where explanation ends.

chapters.title: Pruning Season
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren must decide whether truth redeems or merely explains. With the memoir deadline hours away, she chooses to cut away the false narrative—her publisher's, her own—and drafts the final chapter herself, with Ansel beside her as co-author, not ghost. Emotional beat: agency reclaimed; loyalty to truth over comfort.

chapters.title: A Letter for the Orchard
chapters.summary: Both POV, braided. Spring: the memoir publishes under two names, the orchard blooms, and Ansel nails his old letter to the packing-house door as a vow. Wren answers with a new letter of her own—an invitation to stay. Found family gathers for blossom festival. Emotional beat: resolution as rooting—invisible no more, forgiven, home.
